purpose: Record a chronology finding for candidate 0000065270-26-000005 (Methode Electronics, MEI) so this diligence isn't lost, without pushing it toward acceptance while the confound is unresolved.
finding: Methode Electronics issued two separate GlobeNewswire releases 10 minutes apart on 2026-03-05, both after-hours: 'Methode Electronics Announces Sale of dataMate Business' at 16:20 ET, and 'Methode Electronics, Inc. Reports Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results' at 16:30 ET. Both are on the SEC's frozen candidate's target Item 2.02 8-K date; the results filing itself only reports Item 2.02/9.01, but the market received both pieces of news within the same after-hours window.
why_this_blocks_a_clean_single_catalyst_: Unlike Crane NXT's Antares Vision/De La Rue mentions (which recap already-public news from months earlier), the dataMate divestiture was brand-new, market-moving information disclosed 10 minutes before earnings. Day-1 and likely all subsequent reaction labels for this candidate would reflect BOTH the divestiture and the earnings simultaneously, not earnings alone. This is exactly the kind of same-day competing catalyst the project's standing rules require marking rather than silently attributing to one cause.
disposition: Not excluded, not included -- left quarantined. This is a methodological question (how should NRE represent/label events with a same-day competing catalyst?) that deserves a general, documented policy the way the multi-class-security and foreign-ordinary-shares questions got one, not an ad hoc decision for this single candidate.
recommendation: When a general policy for same-day competing catalysts is designed (likely relevant to Model B's event-clustering requirements described in the master prompt), revisit this candidate. Do not silently drop the dataMate confound if this candidate is picked up again later.
